_comment: Magic items (M8). rarities: how much power an item may have (budget, in points) and what it is worth (value_mult times its base value plus value_add in copper). properties: the whitelist; each has a cost in points per step and what kinds of item may have it ('weapon', 'armor', 'shield', 'jewellery', 'clothing', 'focus'). The AI may only name and describe; code picks the properties and keeps within the budget. cursed_chance: some items are cursed (they cannot be taken off, and carry a hidden flaw) until a temple lifts it. names/stories: built-in words when the AI is not there ({base}, {hero}, {place}, {epithet}, {faction}, {year}).
_attunement: attune_props: an item with any of these needs attunement (a short rest's bond, three at most); so does anything of attune_from rarity or rarer, every artifact and every sentient thing (DMG 2024: most items of real power do). A focus with charges binds only to one who casts spells of their own.

curses.text: It drinks a little of your strength each night.
It whispers, and your aim wavers.
Beasts and dogs hate the smell of it.

_looks: How a magic item looks (worn and held by figures, drawn on the inventory card) when the AI has not chosen: words in its name and story pick its metal, cloth and emblem; its powers (or its rarity) its glow. Every word must be a colour in data/sprites.json figures.
stories: It was made for {hero}, and carried at {place} in {year}.
Taken from the dead at {place}, in the year {year}. The dead did not give it up easily.
{faction} kept it in a locked room for a hundred years, and then lost it.
An old smith's masterwork; the smith was hanged, the story says, for what went into it.
Nobody remembers who made it. Everybody remembers who died holding it.
{hero} carried it at {place} in {year}, and came home, which is more than the others did.
Forged in a bad winter for {faction}. They say it was quenched in snowmelt and blood.
It was buried with {hero} after {place}, and did not stay buried.
Three owners in a single year, in {year}. The third one sold it, and lived.
{faction} paid a fortune for it in {year}, and then paid more to be rid of it.
Found in the river below {place} after the floods of {year}, clean, as if it had been waiting.
It came out of the sack of {place} in {year}, and the soldier who took it never told anyone how.
Made as a wedding gift, the story says. The marriage did not last the year.
{hero} would not let it out of reach, even asleep. Nobody knows what they were afraid of.
It was pawned in {place} in {year} for the price of a winter's bread, and never redeemed.
The smith who made it put a name into the metal, and the name has worn away.
A priest at {place} cursed whoever held it, in {year}, and later blessed it again for a fee.
Given to {hero} by a stranger on the road, they said. They said a lot of things, after.
It was the price of a truce in {year}. The truce did not outlast it.
{faction} swore their oaths on it. Most of those oaths were broken.
It lay in a barrow above {place} for longer than anyone has records, until somebody dug.
Stolen back and forth between two families for three generations. Both families are gone now.
Its last owner died old, in bed, in {year}. Nobody who carried it before can say the same.
_artifact: Artifacts (DMG 2024, chapter 7): rolled once per world on the Artifact Properties tables, [from, to, property] on a d100; count: how many of each kind ([least, most]); a property the game cannot run yet (a creature or a spell level it does not have, a quest only a person could set) is rolled again. properties: what each does, in the game's words; mechanics as item properties (rules/magic.py) or 'on' attunement and dawn effects (game/magic_items.py). destroy: how this world says it can be unmade ({place}, {hero}).

skill.text: Bound to it, you know the craft of {skill} as if you had trained in it.

ward_poison.text: Bound to it, no poison can make you sick.

ward_mind.text: Bound to it, nothing can charm or frighten you.

resist.text: Bound to it, {type} harms you only half as much.

cantrip.text: Bound to it, you can call up {spell} from it whenever you like.

spell_1.text: Bound to it, you can cast {spell} from it; afterwards it is usually spent until dawn.

spell_2.text: Bound to it, you can cast {spell} from it; afterwards it is usually spent until dawn.

spell_3.text: Bound to it, you can cast {spell} from it; afterwards it is usually spent until dawn.

ac.text: Bound to it, blows glance off you a little more often (+1 armour class).

ability.text: Bound to it, your {ability} grows by 2 (to no more than 24).

regeneration.text: Bound to it, your wounds close a little at the start of every turn in a fight, while you still stand.

force.text: Bound to it, every blow or shot that lands carries a jolt of raw force (1d6 more).

speed.text: Bound to it, you move ten feet further each turn.

spell_4.text: Bound to it, you can cast {spell} from it; afterwards it is usually spent until dawn.

spell_5.text: Bound to it, you can cast {spell} from it; afterwards it is usually spent until dawn.

spell_6.text: Bound to it, you can cast {spell} from it; afterwards it is usually spent until dawn.

spell_7.text: Bound to it, you can cast {spell} from it; afterwards it is usually spent until dawn.

ward_senses.text: Bound to it, you cannot be blinded, deafened, turned to stone or stunned.

weak_body.text: Bound to it, your arms and lungs fail you: checks and saves of Strength and Constitution go badly.

weak_mind.text: Bound to it, your will is not wholly your own: saves of Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma go badly.

frail_poison.text: Bound to it, poison does you double harm.

blind_apart.text: Bound to it, you go blind in a fight whenever someone else is carrying it.

deaf_apart.text: Bound to it, you go deaf in a fight whenever someone else is carrying it.

no_smell.text: Bound to it, you smell nothing at all: not bread, not smoke, not rot.

changed_looks.text: Bound to it, your face is not quite your own: people look twice, and do not like what they see.

stench.text: Bound to it, a sour stink hangs about you: creeping up on anyone goes badly.

dulls_jewels.text: Bound to it, stones and jewels lose half their worth when you sell them.

spoils_holy_water.text: Bound to it, holy water near you turns to plain water.

douses_flames.text: Bound to it, torches and lamps around you gutter out: only magic gives you light under the ground.

no_rest_near.text: Bound to it, nobody near you can rest: your companions wake as tired as they lay down.

withers.text: Bound to it, grass browns and leaves curl where your hand falls.

beasts_hate.text: Bound to it, beasts cannot abide you: no animal can be calmed while you are near.

jealous.text: It will not share you: while bound to it, you can bind to nothing else.

drains.text: When you bind to it, it takes something: one of your abilities falls by 2 for good.

shock.text: Binding to it is agony: 8d10 psychic harm, each time.

deadly_bond.text: Each time anyone binds to it, it may kill them outright (a Constitution save, DC 10).

sours_potions.text: Potions carried with it go flat by morning and lose their magic.

blanks_scrolls.text: Scrolls carried with it fade blank by morning.

hated_by.text: Bound to it, every {creature} knows you on sight and will never treat with you.

frail_all.text: Bound to it, every harm does you double.

no_healing.text: Bound to it, you cannot heal: not by rest, not by herbs, not by prayer.

destroy: It can be unmade only in the fire it was forged in, and nobody now living knows where that was.
It breaks, they say, if it is struck with the bones of {hero}, who carried it first.
Drop it into the deepest water under {place}, and it will not come back. Probably.
It will shatter on the day its true name is spoken over it; the name was in a book that burned at {place}.
A smith of the old blood could break it on a cold anvil at midwinter. There may be one left.
It cannot be broken. It can only be given back to whoever it was taken from, and they are long dead.
Bury it with a willing bearer, the stories say, and it sleeps for good.
Melt it in dragon fire, if you can find a dragon willing to oblige.

_sentient: Sentient items (DMG 2024, chapter 7): chance by rarity; Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma 4d6 drop the lowest; alignment, communication and senses on their tables ([from, to, value] on a d100, a d10 and a d4); a special purpose from purposes (what pleases and angers it: tags the game notices); conflict: a Charisma save (DC 12 + its Charisma modifier) and one of the four demands; how it talks, by the way it communicates, in the game's words.

senses: hears, and sees even in darkness, for 120 feet

aligned.name: Aligned
aligned.text: It means to bring down those whose hearts are set against its own.

bane.name: Bane
bane.text: It hates every {creature} and wants them all destroyed.

creator.name: Creator Seeker
creator.text: It wants to find whoever made it, and ask why.

destiny.name: Destiny Seeker
destiny.text: It believes you and it are meant for something great, and it is impatient.

destroyer.name: Destroyer
destroyer.text: It wants blood, any blood, and as often as possible.

glory.name: Glory Seeker
glory.text: It wants to be famous, and you will do.

lore.name: Lore Seeker
lore.text: It hungers for secrets: old books, lost places, forgotten names.

protector.name: Protector
protector.text: It will defend {people} against any harm, and it will not forgive you for harming them.

soulmate.name: Soulmate Seeker
soulmate.text: It is lonely. It wants another thing like itself.

templar.name: Templar
templar.text: It serves {faith}, and it expects you to as well.

demands.keep_close: It wants to be worn or held, always, by you and nobody else.
demands.get_rid: It wants the {thing} gone from the pack.
demands.change: It wants to be carried by someone else in the party.
demands.dreams: It wants its purpose served, now: within a week.

pleased: A warmth runs out of the {item} into your hand. It is pleased.
Something like pride comes off the {item}.
angered: The {item} goes cold as a stone in a river.
A sullen weight: the {item} is angry with you.
The {item} prickles against your skin, resentful.
demand: A want comes out of the {item}, insistent as hunger. {demand}
The {item} pulls at you like a child at a sleeve. {demand}

pleased: "Now you are learning," says the {item}, quite clearly.
The {item} laughs, low, and says nothing more.
angered: "Coward," says the {item}, loud enough for the others to hear.
The {item} says, coldly: "I have had better bearers. Dead ones."
"Is this what I am for?" the {item} asks. You do not answer.
demand: "I will say this once," says the {item}. {demand}

pleased: A voice inside your skull, pleased: yes.
You feel the {item} smile, somewhere behind your eyes.
A thought that is not yours: good. We go on.
angered: A voice in your head, very quiet: you shame us both.
The {item}'s anger presses behind your eyes like a headache.
A thought that is not yours, cold and clear: I will remember this.
demand: A voice in your head, patient and terrible. {demand}

sentient.withheld: The {item} withholds its power until you do as it asks.
sentient.seized: The {item} reaches into {name}'s mind and takes hold: for hours, {name} will fight as it wills.
sentient.satisfied: The {item} is quiet again: it has what it wanted.
